{{Quote|It is a technique that is almost as old as the Sith themselves&hellip;it is a means of severing connections between life, the Force, and feeding upon the death it causes. It cannot be taught&hellip;it can only be gained through instinct, through experiencing its effects, first-hand.|Kreia|<ref name="KOTOR2" />}}
'''Force drain''' referred to a spectrum of offensive and defensive [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]], tied to the same concept, which used the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to feed upon a life essence of an organic target. Mastery of each technique could scale the area of effect, sometimes dramatically, or exhaust the victims almost instantaneously.

==Description==
{{Quote|As much as one may use the Force to bolster the wills and strengths of others, the reverse is possible, though not often used. Instead of sending one's will through connections in the Force, instead such connections are drawn upon, fed upon, and drained completely.|Kreia|<ref name="KOTOR2" />}}
Force abilities such as '''drain life''' and '''dark healing''',<ref name="Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> siphoned vitality to sometimes offer an equivalent effect of [[Force healing/Legends|Force healing]], the difference being that the regenerative processes in the user was fueled draining the targets. Other techniques like '''drain Force''' rekindled [[The Force/Legends|Force energy]] in the user, offensively draining the Force energy from those whom the power was turned upon.<ref name="KOTOR2" /> 

The essence of the Force drain was in exploiting [[The Force/Legends|Force]] connections which bind the universe together, drawing upon them until they were drained completely, which killed the exhausted life.<ref name="KOTOR2" /> Having personal connections involved, however, could obstruct the use of this ability; for example, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] discovered that it was very difficult to use Force drain on close family members.<ref name="DES">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Using Force connections to feed on the life energy of others was addictive, and it also amplified the ability to sense and seek out those strong with the Force, feeding on their presence.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

According to [[Kreia]], the technique of Force drain could not be taught but only be gained through instinct, through experiencing its effects first-hand,<ref name="KOTOR2 Meetra" /> which sometimes left in the victims an irreversible need turned into hunger, eventually compelling them to feed themselves. Due to this, multiple various forms of the power existed, performed by adepts of the [[Dark side of the Force|Dark Side]] across time.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

[[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] was able to create a spherical '''death field''' of pure [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] energy around himself that instantly withered away anyone unlucky enough to be caught within its radius. However, this ability was extremely exhausting, to the point where it was highly impractical for Bane to use it unaided.<ref name="Bane3" /> Another application was '''Force Diminish''', which was a Force power that enabled the user to cause damage to an opponent's health and vitality. With enough concentration, the user was able to weaken an opponent's body and mind to the point of death.{{Fact}}

===Mass Force drain===
[[File:Ziost_dying.png|thumb|240x240px|Darth Vitiate consumes Ziost]]
Several adepts of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark Side]] achieved such mastery over Force drain, that they could use it to consume entire planets. A [[Sith Emperor's ritual|technique]] developed by [[Tenebrae]], as well as the ''Hunger'' of [[Darth Nihilus]], left whole worlds barren and lifeless, completely destroying all life and the very Force presence on their surfaces. Performed correctly, such application of the Force drain could significantly fuel Dark Lord's powers, or even grant them immortality.<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref>  However with the death of the applicant, planets could be restored by themselves, with the [[The Force|Force]] rushing in to fill the unnatural void, as it happened on [[Nathema]].<ref name="nathema conspiracy">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|The Nathema Conspiracy}}</ref>

Massive application of the Force drain could also be focused on a specific species,<ref name="DA">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref> or even be spread in time, allowing the user to continuously feed of their surroundings, without necessarily devastating the whole world at once.<ref name="DES" /> 

== History ==
[[File:RevanForceDrain.png|thumb|right|300px|Darth Revan, wielder of Force drain]]
The arcane practice was known to the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and came into use at some point after the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]].<ref name="KOTOR2 Kreia">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'': [[Kreia]] states that the technique is almost as old as the Sith, so it must have come into use after the foundation of their Order.</ref> Supposedly, the technique was pioneered by a mysterious individual known only as [[Zelashiel]] the Blasphemer. It was lost over time, however, as the Lords of the Sith abandoned [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] space and their strongholds were deserted.<ref name="KOTOR2 Meetra">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'': Telepathic dialog with [[Kreia]], triggered the first time [[Meetra Surik]] kills one of the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] she went in search of (non-canon dark side path.)</ref> 

In [[3996 BBY]],<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], the Dark Lord in the time of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], performed a ritual to drain life from thousands of [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]], so that his [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] could endure for [[11 ABY/Legends|more than four thousand years]] in the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="DA" />

===Old Sith Wars===
[[Revan]] learned the technique from [[Zelashiel]]'s teachings, redocumenting them in his own [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|Holocron]].<ref name="BoS" /> Revan's apprentice, Dark Lord [[Darth Malak]] was able to drain life energy and force energy simultaneously, as he did in the [[Battle of Rakata Prime|last battle]] of the [[Jedi Civil War]] as he dueled his former master.<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> Revan's Holocron was later discovered by [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], who learned many Sith powers of old from it.<ref name="Bane">[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]</ref>
[[File:RevanForceDrain.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Traya draining the Jedi High Council of their life force energy]]
Near the end of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], Revan learned within the [[Trayus Academy]] how to take advantage of [[Wound in the Force/Legends|Wounds in the Force]], located in places drained of life, and how to make them, in order to break the will of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and turn them to the dark side. The academy was later used by the [[Sith Triumvirate]], members of which were all proficient in the art of Force drain. Triumvirate's leader, [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], used it on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], to consume the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] in the persons of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Vrook Lamar]], [[Kavar]], and [[Zez-Kai Ell]], who were assembled in the ruins of the [[Jedi Enclave]] by [[Meetra Surik]] to answer the Sith threat.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

As detrimental as the teachings of the dark side were said to be to the very flesh of their practitioners, Force drain could be more dangerous still, if one over-relied on the technique or did not contain its full measure of power. During the [[First Jedi Purge]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Nihilus]], another member of the [[Sith Triumvirate]], took this practice to unmatched levels and honed a pernicious means of ''feeding upon the Force'', which eventually enslaved him. His ''Hunger'' transformed Nihilus into a walking void in the Force, unable to close itself no matter how much he consumed. <ref name="KOTOR2" />

[[File:Katarrdevastation.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Nihilus's grandiose display of "feeding upon the Force"]]

In [[3952 BBY]],<ref name="Jedi vs Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[Darth Nihilus]] gave one of the most grandiose displays of the Force drain, when he [[Conclave at Katarr|consumed]] [[Katarr/Legends|Katarr]], a [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] world in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. Unchecked, the addictive use of his talent would have ultimately cost his life had he not been slain by [[Meetra Surik]],<ref name="UU">{{Tales|24|Unseen, Unheard}}</ref> a Jedi similar to Nihilus in that she was also a living [[Wound in the Force/Legends|Force Wound]]. However, whereas Nihilus had been forced to use the technique as a matter of survival on [[Malachor V]], Surik never consciously utilized the ability, and as such never became dependent on it. She could however, subconsciously use her condition to feed off the deaths of people around her. She ended up incidentally using this to accelerate the restoration of her ability to use the Force after she [[Sever Force/Legends|severed]] her connection to it at the conclusion of the [[Battle of Malachor V]].<ref name="KOTOR2" />

During the [[Dark Wars]], Force drain was taught to a sect of [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassins]], one of Revan's elite [[Jedi hunter/Legends|Jedi hunter]] squads, to track Jedi more efficiently through their presence in the Force. On [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]], during the [[Battle of Onderon (Onderon Civil War)|Second Battle of Onderon]], the Sith tried to bolster their forces by feeding on a [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] located in the [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd]].<ref name="KOTOR2" />

===Sith Emperor===
[[File:Ritual of Nathema.png|thumb|Nathema, drained of life|209x209px]]
At the same time, Revan discovered the remnant of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|old Sith Empire]], where the teachings of the Force drain had not been forgotten. Almost a thousand years before [[Darth Nihilus|Nihilus]], in [[4999 BBY]], Sith [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Tenebrae]] used his own [[Sith Emperor's ritual|version]] of the Force drain on [[Nathema]], in a [[Ritual of Nathema|ritual]] that granted him immortality through [[Death/Legends|death]] of all living things on the planet, including thousands of other [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]].<ref name="Revan" /> When his own [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Empire]] [[Great Galactic War|invaded]] the [[The galaxy/Legends|Galaxy]] in [[3681 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> deathroll fueled his powers allowing for a new [[Emperor's ritual crisis|ritual]] of an even larger scale; however this time he was [[Dromund Kaas operation|stopped]] by a [[Hero of Tython|Jedi Knight]], who destroyed the Emperor's physical body.<ref name="TOR:Doomsday">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Doomsday|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref>

Hoping to bring the now-incorporeal [[Tenebrae|Emperor]] back, to be properly killed, [[Revan]], still alive after centuries of stasis, attempted to perform a different kind of Force drain ritual on the [[Yavin 4/Legends|fourth moon]] of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]], in the ancient Sith temple known as the [[Temple of Sacrifice]]. The ritual was stopped by an invading [[Yavin Coalition]], but the spirit of the Emperor did fuel himself on the deaths on the moon nevertheless, and reemerged,<ref name="The Enemy Within">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The Enemy Within|[[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]}}</ref> using his own [[Sith Emperor's ritual|drain Ritual]] on a planet of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], [[Ziost crisis|devastating]] it the same way as [[Nathema]], and fueling himself even more.<ref name="The End of It All">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The End of It All|Ziost}}</ref>

===Age of the New Republic===
[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] fed off the inhabitants of his retreat world of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] collectively with his [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]], although those unfortunates were drained slowly, over a long period of time, rather than consumed with the whole world at once.<ref name="DES" /> 

During the [[Disciples of Ragnos crisis]], some of the [[New Reborn]] were able to use Force drain as well, and members of the New Jedi Order were permitted to employ this power on their enemies.<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

[[Darth Krayt]] used this power on his ally Luke Skywalker and their mutual enemy Abeloth in 44 ABY, though he suffered as they did. This was not an act of treachery on the part of the Sith Lord, however, as he only drained Luke as the Jedi Grandmaster was too close to Abeloth, an action Skywalker accepted as needed once he understood this.<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:JediExilekillingZezKaiEll.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] uses Force drain to kill Zez-Kai Ell (non-canon).]]
In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', if the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] followed the path of the dark side she would have instinctively learned to consume the Force feeding on the Jedi Masters she went in search of, but since [[canon]]ically she followed the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]], the Exile would not know such a technique&mdash;yet she bore the same sort of hunger due to her innate [[Force-bond/Legends|Force bonding]] ability and severed connection to the Force, and she grew stronger the more connections she formed during her journeys, causing the Masters to believe her the true threat behind what had befallen the Jedi.

''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' states that Force drain cannot be performed on sentient beings. However, Kreia states otherwise, which is later proven by Darth Nihilus in ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords''. In addition, Force drain's variant Death Field was used by Darth Bane in Dynasty of Evil.
